title: Transnasal Administration of Surfactant Aerosol to the Lungs of Infants Using Direct Interfaces - Lessons Learned from Computational Fluid Dynamics.
authors: Jubaer, Hasan; Farkas, Dale; Dalton, Caleb; Momin, Mohammad A M; Hindle, Michael; Longest, Worth
one_liner_zh: 该文用计算流体力学优化婴儿经鼻表面活性剂气溶胶递送系统，对象为气溶胶颗粒与呼吸道几何，不涉及无序蛋白、PPI或相分离，方法虽为物理模拟但无可迁移的互作机制建模启发。
abstract: PURPOSE: Direct-to-infant (D2I) transnasal aerosol surfactant therapy (AST) offers a promising non-invasive alternative for treating neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). However, achieving high lung delivery efficiency with dry powder inhalers (DPIs) requires careful optimization of complex fluid-particle interactions. This study used computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to optimize an Infant Air‑Jet Dry Powder Aerosol Delivery System (iDP‑ADS) and derive transferable design principles. METHODS: A CFD model of the iDP‑ADS coupled to a 31‑week preterm nose‑throat geometry was validated against in vitro measurements. Sensitivity analyses evaluated modeling assumptions (steady‑state vs. transient, monodisperse vs. polydisperse) and critical design parameters influencing aerosol delivery, such as upstream air volume, interface geometry, temporal aerosol emission profiles, and actuation flow rates. RESULTS: The CFD model demonstrated strong in vitro agreement (2.8% mean absolute difference). Regarding modeling: standard simplifications, particularly steady-state approximations, overpredicted lung transmission (~24%), establishing the necessity of high-fidelity transient simulations with polydisperse aerosols. Regarding aerosol delivery: integrating an upstream air volume created "hydrodynamic shielding," reducing relative interface losses by up to 50%. A 10 mm diffusive path length and 20 degrees  (inward and downward) prong alignment balanced jet dissipation while minimizing nasal deposition. Front-loading of aerosol emission prevented entrapment of 10-14% of the dose in anatomical dead space. An optimal system-specific actuation flow rate of 3 L/min achieved ~53.5% aerosol lung transmission, balancing aerosolization efficiency against turbulence-driven transport losses. CONCLUSIONS: High-efficiency transnasal AST requires balancing often competing aerosol generation physics, transport behavior, and clinical constraints. This study highlights CFD as a vital design tool, providing key lessons to inform future modeling and practical interface development.
abstract_zh: 目的：直接对婴儿（D2I）经鼻气溶胶表面活性剂治疗（AST）为新生儿呼吸窘迫综合征（RDS）提供了一种有前景的无创替代方案。然而，使用干粉吸入器（DPIs）实现高肺部递送效率需要仔细优化复杂的流体-颗粒相互作用。本研究采用计算流体动力学（CFD）优化婴儿空气喷射干粉气溶胶递送系统（iDP‑ADS），并推导出可转移的设计原则。方法：将iDP‑ADS的CFD模型与31周早产儿鼻咽几何结构耦合，并针对体外测量进行验证。敏感性分析评估了建模假设（稳态与瞬态、单分散与多分散）以及影响气溶胶递送的关键设计参数，如上游空气体积、接口几何结构、时间气溶胶发射曲线和驱动流量。结果：CFD模型与体外实验表现出高度一致性（平均绝对差异2.8%）。关于建模：标准简化，特别是稳态近似，高估了肺部传输（约24%），确立了高保真瞬态模拟与多分散气溶胶的必要性。关于气溶胶递送：整合上游空气体积产生了“流体动力学屏蔽”，将相对接口损失减少高达50%。10 mm扩散路径长度和20度（向内和向下）叉头对齐在喷射耗散与最小化鼻腔沉积之间取得平衡。气溶胶发射的前置加载防止了10-14%的剂量滞留在解剖死腔中。系统特定的最优驱动流量为3 L/min，实现了约53.5%的气溶胶肺部传输，在雾化效率与湍流驱动传输损失之间取得平衡。结论：高效经鼻AST需要平衡通常相互竞争的气溶胶生成物理、传输行为和临床约束。本研究强调CFD作为关键设计工具，为未来建模和实际接口开发提供了重要经验。
